walkthroughs.body_html:
Exchange & Transport — a core area of A-Level Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Exchange & Transport brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Exchange & Transport.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Water potential of pure water is:
options: +1.0 kPa
0 kPa
−100 kPa

mcqs.q: What distinguishes active transport from facilitated diffusion?
options: Water moves towards the sugar because sugar attracts water molecules chemically.
Both move substances down a concentration gradient, but active transport is faster.
Active transport requires energy (ATP) and can move substances against the concentration gradient.
Active transport only happens in animals and facilitated diffusion only in plants.

mcqs.q: How is sucrose loaded into the phloem at a source?
options: Water moves towards the sugar because sugar attracts water molecules chemically.
Sucrose is pushed into the phloem by turgor pressure from leaf cells.
Sucrose diffuses passively into the phloem because it is more concentrated outside.
By active transport (using ATP) via companion cells, against a concentration gradient.

mcqs.q: In osmosis, which direction does water move?
options: Sucrose is pushed into the phloem by turgor pressure from leaf cells.
Water moves towards the sugar because sugar attracts water molecules chemically.
From a region of higher water potential (less concentrated solution) to lower water potential.
Water moves from high solute concentration to low solute concentration.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Active transport”?
options: Movement of substances against a gradient by carrier proteins using ATP.
Net movement of water from higher to lower water potential across a partially permeable membrane.
Membrane is a phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins that move laterally; cholesterol stabilises it.
Coupled movement of one substance with another (e.g. Na⁺ with glucose) using a carrier protein.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Facilitated diffusion”?
options: Net movement of water from higher to lower water potential across a partially permeable membrane.
Coupled movement of one substance with another (e.g. Na⁺ with glucose) using a carrier protein.
Net movement of particles down a concentration gradient; passive, no ATP.
Passive transport of polar/large molecules through channel or carrier proteins down a gradient.
